newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada to tighten tax rules for emigrants.
newsitem.headline: Canada to tighten tax rules for emigrants.

text.p: Canada on Wednesday announced changes to income tax rules for people who leave the country aimed at ensuring that all gains from property transferred out of the country are subject to Canadian income tax.

"From now on, all emigrants, including trusts, will be subject to Canadian tax on any gains they have accrued up to the time of departure, other than on Canadian real estate and a limited group of other assets, which Canada always retains the right to tax," Finance Minister Paul Martin said.

Until now, emigrants from Canada were not taxed on gains on certain Canadian property at the time they left. Under the new rules, people who leave the country will calculate their tax as if they had disposed of all their property except Canadian real estate and some business property.

Emigrants will be able to pay the tax immediately, or leave a security deposit with Revenue Canada for payment at a later date. Emigrants with "significant" property, including real estate, will have to report it to Revenue Canada before they leave. People who have only been in Canada temporarily will not be subject to the new taxes.
